newsitem.title: UK: UK funds see limited Labour effect on stocks - poll.
newsitem.headline: UK funds see limited Labour effect on stocks - poll.

text.p: The majority of UK fund managers expect a Labour election victory to have little effect on equities over the next five years despite concerns over tax and inflation, according to a poll commissioned by Merrill Lynch.

The Gallup survey of fund managers' expectations for a Labour government showed that bad news on corporate tax appeared to have been priced into the market, although risks would mount as parliament progressed.
If Labour won the election, 60 percent of managers expect the performance of the equity market to be broadly the same over 12 months as under a re-elected Conservative government.
"There are greater doubts about the outlook for the equity market over the next five years," it said.
Over five years, 35 percent of fund managers expect a poorer equity market showing under Labour against 56 percent who see a Labour win making little difference.
A clear majority expect Labour to increase corporation tax rates, reduce ACT and increase employers' National Insurance Contributions.

Respondents were virtually evenly split between those who expected higher inflation under Labour and those who believed there would be little difference compared with what a Conservative government would deliver, the survey said.
But it added that there were few optimists about the prospects for inflation under Labour. "...the market remains concerned that inflation may surprise on the upside under a Labour government."
A majority of fund managers do not expect Labour to take Britain into EMU over the next five years.
The survey was carried out between April 7 and 9, the fourth week of the election campaign.
